learning: If slalom and s-bend losses fall below 0.9 per run with oscillation at or below 0.3, keep the span and move to gain tuning for progress. If losses persist with oscillation at or below 0.3, the next geometry test is sensor_size 0.016 m at this span. If oscillation exceeds 0.3, the wider centroid is too smooth or too sensitive, so revert to ±0.05 m and test footprint size.
notes: Single-variable test: outer sensors widened from ±0.05 m to ±0.06 m on the iteration 2 baseline, with the iteration 2 controller unchanged.
rationale: The Builder's proposal is the iteration 2 baseline (y 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, 12 mm footprints) with the outer sensors widened to x = ±0.06 m and inner sensors at ±0.03 m, spacing 3 cm. The evidence favours keeping the iteration 2 controller unchanged. Iteration 2 (score 124.6) is the best race so far. Iteration 3 showed that wheel_track 0.10 m cut oval progress from 0.51 to 0.14 without fixing slalom losses, so the track stays at 0.12 m. Iteration 4 showed that forward sensing at y 0.06 m cut oval progress to 0.20 and left slalom at 1.0 loss per run, so the sensors stay at y 0.04 m. Weights stay at [-2,-1,0,1,2] and the controller stays at kp 1.0, kd 0.2, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.0 and last_direction. This isolates the single geometry change, the outer span. Steering oscillation was 0.23 to 0.27 in iteration 2, so a wider centroid may raise it, and the controller is kept as is to measure that effect cleanly. Expected: slalom and s-bend line losses below 0.9 per run, max_error below 0.06 m on tight bends, oscillation at or below 0.3, and oval progress near 0.45 or higher.
